answer: An agent network trading saffron futures mitigates Sybil attacks through trust-graph propagation. At the dawn of each epoch, the protocol computes bounded random walks from anchor nodes to score every agent vertex. An attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of acquiring organic inbound trust edges across the network bottleneck cut. However, this mechanism penalizes benign newcomers with severe cold-start latency and remains susceptible to targeted collusion.
